claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 10 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation with Alex.

**Do you live with Alex, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He doesn't live with me - he lives with someone else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your situation better.

**Are you paying towards Alex's upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, or contributions towards his accommodation), and if so, how much do you contribute and how often?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his needs - things like clothes and other essentials. I give about £20 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

According to the rules, you can still qualify for Child Benefit even if your child lives with someone else, as long as you're contributing to their upkeep by at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment would be.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have a few more questions to complete my assessment.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just one more question to complete my assessment:

**What is the current Child Benefit rate? Or to put it another way - do you know if your £20 per week contribution is at least equal to what the Child Benefit payment would be for one child?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure what the current rate is, to be honest. Is my £20 a week enough?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand you're not certain about the current Child Benefit rates. Based on the information you've provided, let me assess your situation:

You are:
- Responsible for Alex (your 10-year-old son)
- Living in the UK
- Contributing £20 per week towards his upkeep (clothes and essentials)
- Alex lives with someone else
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

The key issue here is whether your £20 weekly contribution meets or exceeds the Child Benefit rate for one child. According to the rules, when a child lives with someone else, you can continue to get Child Benefit beyond the initial 8 weeks if you contribute to your child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment.

However, without knowing the exact current Child Benefit rate and whether your £20 per week meets that threshold, I cannot make a definitive determination of your eligibility.
